title: Move to a new phone: approve on the old phone
summary: On the old phone, after the check code: warns that the new phone gets full access, shows the time of the request, waits through the cooldown, asks for the biometric check and opens the MAS consent page in a private web view, where the user checks the new phone's model and place and approves (ADR 0059, ADR 0118). The SDK then sends cross-signing and the backup key to the new phone.

phase.description: warning: the full-access warning with the time of the request and the cooldown. confirmIdentity: the biometric check (rule 14, tier 3). loading, consent, finishing, done and failed: as link-computer-approve.

requestedAt.description: When the new phone scanned the code (GrantGeneratedQrLoginProgress.qrScanned), shown as the local time with bipe_app_link_phone_time.

secondsLeft.description: Cooldown left, from registries/accounts.json webLinkCooldownSeconds to 0.

place.description: Approximate place of the new phone's IP from GET /v1/web-link/place, as in link-computer-approve. Empty when the server does not know it.

error.description: String key of the failed phase: bipe_link_computer_error_sign_in, bipe_app_link_phone_expired or bipe_error_generic.

appear.effect: Plays the web_link_warning haptic and starts the countdown from the start, also when the screen comes back to the front.

continue.effect: Only when secondsLeft is 0. Sets confirmIdentity.

confirmIdentity.effect: Asks for the approval owner check (bipe#785, security.md rules 5 and 14): biometrics only, with no passcode fallback (Android: BIOMETRIC_STRONG, class 3); a phone with no biometrics set up asks for the Bipe PIN (bipe_pin_enter_title), checked by POST /v1/me/pin/check, where wrong tries count against the account (bipe_pin_wrong with tries left, bipe_pin_blocked_body); a phone with no screen lock is refused and the flow goes back. bipe_app_link_phone_biometric is the biometric reason. On a pass, reads the hidden password and opens the MAS page as link-computer-approve open. On a fail or cancel, back to warning.

isLoginForm.description: The page has a form with a password field (the MAS login form).

isConsentPage.description: The path is /device/<id> and the page has a form.

pageLoaded.effect: As link-computer-approve pageLoaded: fills the MAS login form once with the hidden password, looks up the place on the consent page, and calls ContinuationMessageSender.confirm when the user leaves the consent page.

update.description: The GrantGeneratedQrLoginProgress case that onUpdate got.

progress.effect: syncingSecrets: finishing. done: sets done and shows bipe_app_link_phone_done.

reason.description: The HumanQrGrantLoginError case that GrantLoginWithQrCodeHandler.generate threw.

taskFailed.effect: expired and notFound → bipe_app_link_phone_expired; cancelled after the consent page → closes with no message (the user declined on the MAS page); anything else → bipe_error_generic. Calls finish.

finish.effect: As link-computer-approve finish: clears the web view, then POST /v1/web-link/finish so that bipe-api ends the MAS browser session the web view made.

cancel.effect: In warning: ContinuationMessageSender.cancel and closes the flow. The new phone does not sign in.

newCode.effect: From failed: closes this screen and opens link-phone-show again with a new code.

notes: ADR 0059 QR approval: before the old phone approves, it shows the new phone's model, approximate place and time and asks for a biometric check. Time: requestedAt on the warning. Model: the MAS consent page shows the client name and the user agent of the new phone (recovery-old-phone sets both with the phone model, ADR 0118 F6). Place: GET /v1/web-link/place for the IP on the MAS page, shown above it as in link-computer-approve. The approve button is on the MAS page, after all three are on screen.

Why a web view: MAS approves a device code grant only on its consent page (ADR 0118). This screen reuses the link-computer-approve web view, form fill, place lookup and finish as they are; only the strings and the first phase differ.
History: syncingSecrets passes cross-signing and the backup key to the new phone, so it decrypts the history itself and needs no recovery key or other approval (bipe-chat/bipe#201).

The hidden password stays on the old phone (ADR 0059). The new phone signs in through MAS with its own OAuth session and has no hidden password; link-computer-scan then shows needsPin on the new phone until it gets one.
Unverified (24 October 2026): that the MAS consent page shows the client name of a device code grant; the full flow between two phones and between two Simulators.
